scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees (Erasmus Mundus Catalogue)

existing.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are master's degrees jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, plus academic and non-academic associated partners. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, maintained by EACEA and updated annually, lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU; the stored row corresponds to the catalogue's Sweden country facet. Master's-level students from all over the world may apply, and Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available for outstanding students at participating programmes. Applicants apply directly to the consortium running their chosen programme, not to the European Commission.
eligibility: Hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in the last year of bachelor studies
Graduate before the master's programme starts
Or demonstrate a bachelor's equivalent level of learning officially recognised according to national legislation and practices in the degree awarding country
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in the final year of bachelor studies, and must graduate before the master's programme starts; a demonstrably equivalent level of learning officially recognised in the degree-awarding country is also accepted.
benefits: Joint degree or multiple degrees from consortium institutions
requirements: Application submitted directly to the consortium running the chosen programme
Entry requirements are set by each master's own website
All steps of the application process (with and without scholarship) are published by each master's website
application_method: Search the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue for a suitable programme
Contact the consortium directly for courses, application procedures and scholarship availability
Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme
existing.selection_notes: Scholarships are awarded to the best-ranked students; each consortium publishes its own entry requirements and selection process.
existing.application_period: Applications for courses starting the following academic year are submitted between October and January; the exact date is set by each consortium.
existing.deadline_display: In most cases you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
existing.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) - jointly designed master's delivered by a consortium
